summary: Instructions for building AAPS on the Linux command line without Android Studio: install a JDK and the Android command-line tools, generate a keystore with keytool, compile with the Gradle wrapper, and sign the APK with apksigner. No app screens are involved.

sections.heading: Build instructions for the command-line
sections.summary: Page title and a note that this method is for users comfortable with the command line and git.

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.summary: Installing OpenJDK and the Android command-line tools, setting ANDROID_HOME and PATH, and accepting SDK licences.

sections.heading: Building AAPS with Gradle wrapper
sections.summary: Heading for the three build steps.

sections.heading: 1. Generate a Java keystore file for signing AAPS
sections.summary: Creating a signing keystore with keytool, or reusing an existing one.

sections.heading: 2. Compile the AAPS APK file
sections.summary: Cloning the repository and running the Gradle task that produces the unsigned APK.

sections.heading: 3. Create a signed APK file from the unsigned one
sections.summary: Signing the APK with apksigner so it can be installed.
